text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Latvia is among six ex-Soviet republics and 15 African states to have lost the right to vote at U.N. meetings because of a debt of almost $2.1 million.

- Deloitte & Touche, liquidators of the collpased Bank Baltija, announced it will request the bank's money from Finhold Ltd., an off-shore company created by Bank Baltija's ex-chief Alexander Lavent, to which bank assets were transferred.
- Talks between Russia and Latvia on the delimitation of their land border are due to resume today in Moscow after more than a three-month break.
- In January the number of unemployed increased from 7.2 to 7.3 percent.
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele and German ambassador Horst Veisel signed two intergovernmental agreements on Friday.
- Party Fatherland & Freedom criticises Latvian parliament speaker Alfred Chepanis for his stand in recent talks held in Moscow.
- One more Latvian bank, Latvijas privatbanka, had its licence annulled by the Bank of Latvia.
